steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren climbed the spiral stairs for the ten-thousandth time, her hand trailing the cold iron railing like greeting an old friend.

The storm had been building since noon. She could tell by the way the gulls went quiet first — they always knew before the clouds did.

She lit the lamp.

Below, through the glass, the sea was turning the color of a bruise. Somewhere out in that darkness, she imagined a ship. A captain squinting through rain. A young sailor on his first voyage, terrified and pretending otherwise.

She had never met any of them. That was the whole point.

For thirty-one years, Maren had tended this light for strangers she would never know, steering them around rocks she had memorized like her own heartbeat. No thank-you notes reached the lighthouse. No names. Just the quiet knowledge, each morning, that the harbor was full.

Her daughter had once asked if she was lonely.

Maren had thought about it seriously, the way the question deserved.

*"I keep the light,"* she'd finally said. *"Someone always needs it."*

The lamp turned. The storm arrived. The beam swept out across the black water — patient, steady, faithful —

and somewhere beyond the dark, a ship turned safely home.
